episodes.title: THE DISTANCE CHANGED FIRST
episodes.caption:
Nothing moved.

Earth remained where it was.
The Moon remained where it was.

But the space beyond them stretched into something our maps could no longer measure.

The first anomaly wasn't an object.

It was distance itself.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-AUG-001
episodes.comment:
SPATIAL NOTE:

The distortion crosses the background starfield without hiding it.

Light bends along both edges.

Whatever changed here may not be occupying space.

It may be changing space.
episodes.prompt:
Use the approved starter frame as the opening composition: Earth in the lower-left area, the Moon nearby, and a gigantic dark spatial distortion stretching upward through space. Create a 10-second vertical cinematic shot.

0–2s: Start almost still. Earth and Moon appear normal. The dark spatial rift looms in the background. Camera slowly pushes in.

2–5s: The background stars begin to warp more noticeably along both edges of the distortion. Space itself seems to stretch. Earth and Moon remain visually stable, but the area beyond them looks like the distance is being pulled apart.

5–8s: The invisible distortion intensifies. Light bends harder. The apparent gap between Earth and the deep background subtly expands in an impossible way, as if space is elongating rather than objects moving.

8–10s: End on the strongest moment of spatial tension: the cosmic rift towering over Earth, starfields distorted and elongated, with the sense that distance itself has changed. Keep the source unseen. No creature reveal. Preserve awe and realism.

episodes.title: THE GAP REFUSED TO CLOSE
episodes.caption:
Every fragment was moving.

Thousands of rocks drifted inward from both sides.

But the darkness between them never became smaller.

The debris could enter the region.

The distance couldn't.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-AUG-002
episodes.comment:

The surrounding debris continues to behave normally until it reaches the boundary.

The empty region maintains the same width.

2–5s: Small and medium asteroids from both sides begin drifting inward toward the dark gap. Motion is smooth and believable, like gravity is acting on them.

5–8s: More debris moves inward, but the central darkness never shrinks. Rocks approach the boundary, curve or slide past, while the empty region maintains the same width.

8–10s: The asteroid motion becomes unmistakable: everything is moving, but the gap refuses to close. End on the impossible stillness of the central void. No text, no reveal of a visible object inside it.

episodes.caption:
At first, there was nothing to photograph.

Then the galaxies behind it began to bend.

Light curved around an empty region thousands of times larger than the planet beside it.

Something was there.

We just couldn't see the thing itself.

episodes.comment:

Multiple background sources bend around the same region.

There is mass where the image shows nothing.

episodes.title: THE AURORA POINTED OUTWARD
episodes.caption:
Earth's aurora normally follows the planet.

This time, it reached away from it.

Across the night side, every stream stretched toward the same dark point above Earth.

Something outside the atmosphere was pulling on the field.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-AUG-004
episodes.comment:

The displacement appeared across a region too large to be explained by a local disturbance.

Every visible stream shares the same orientation.

The source appears to be beyond Earth.

Use the approved starter frame with Earth and abnormal aurora behavior. Create a 10-second vertical cinematic shot.

episodes.title: EVERY SATELLITE TURNED AT ONCE
episodes.caption:
One satellite turned.

Then another.

Then hundreds more.

Different orbits.
Different systems.
Different operators.

Every instrument ended up facing the same place.

And none of them received the command to do it.

COLOSSUS SIGNAL // CS-AUG-005
episodes.comment:
ORBITAL NOTE:

The satellites did not leave their assigned trajectories.

Only their orientation changed.

Whatever attracted their instruments was far beyond Earth.

We still cannot identify it.
episodes.prompt:
Use the approved starter frame as the opening composition: Earth centered below, a huge anomaly in the upper-right distance, and many satellites in different normal orientations. Create a 10-second vertical shot.

0–2s: Start with the satellite swarm mostly behaving normally. Only one satellite begins a subtle rotation toward the distant anomaly. Camera slowly drifts forward.

2–4s: A second and third satellite begin turning. The rest still face their original directions. Keep the motion readable and sequential.

4–7s: The turning spreads through the orbital field. More satellites rotate one after another, not instantly. Earth remains steady below, the anomaly looming far away.

7–10s: By the final moment, nearly every visible satellite has reoriented toward the same point in space. End on the eerie unified alignment. This is the payoff. No arrows, no graphics, no text.

episodes.title: IT FINALLY CLEARED THE PLANET
episodes.caption:
For days, the planet hid most of the structure.

Then it moved.

Not the planet.

The thing behind it.

For the first time, nothing blocked our view.

We could see the entire body.

And the planet beside it looked small.

No propulsion system has been identified.

Same shape.
Same spacing.
Same brightness.

Those two groups of stars were nowhere near each other.

Then we noticed the darkness between them.

episodes.caption:

Then another.

Then four more.

Six enormous pulses.

Six different directions.

One destination.

Earth.

episodes.comment:

For the first time, the pattern appears centered on Earth.

episodes.title: THE ASTEROID BELT OPENED A LANE
episodes.caption:
The asteroids didn't scatter.

They moved aside.

Thousands of objects slowly separated into two walls…

leaving an empty corridor through the middle.

Nothing had entered it yet.

Something was being given a path.

episodes.comment:

No collision initiated the movement.

Objects on opposite sides changed course in coordinated directions.

The corridor continues beyond the observed field.

Its destination is unknown.

5–8s: Larger asteroids respond and move aside with slow heavy inertia. The central path progressively widens and extends farther into deep space.

episodes.title: SOMETHING STOPPED IT
episodes.caption:
The first one reached for the Moon.

Its hand was almost there.

Then another colossal body entered the frame.

It caught the arm before it could touch the surface.

Neither of them looked at Earth.

That was when we understood.

They are not all on the same side.

episodes.comment:

It made no movement toward Earth afterward.

We do not know whether it protected the Moon…

or prevented the other entity from taking it.
